summary.name: Featherview
summary.one_liner: Featherview is a free, open-source, keyboard-driven image viewer for macOS that also batch-converts and resizes images.
use_cases: flip through a folder of photos and cull rejects
batch convert HEIC photos to WebP or JPEG
resize and rename a set of images for sharing
view layered Photoshop, GIMP or Procreate files without an editor
view legacy image formats such as PCX, XPM or FITS
check camera exposure and location info for a photo
summary.what_it_does: Featherview opens a single image or a whole folder in one window, with single-key navigation, rotation, zoom, trashing and full screen. Rotating JPEG, HEIC and TIFF is lossless. Its batch mode lets you choose output format, size and file naming pattern, add steps such as resize, crop, colour fixes, border, text or watermark, and save those settings as presets. It reads many formats macOS does not handle natively, including PCX, QOI, FITS, and flattened layered files from Photoshop, GIMP, Krita and Procreate. Press I to show a histogram and camera, exposure and location info, which is worked out locally.
notable: Open source and free, installable via Homebrew cask
Batch conversion never overwrites originals and skips unreadable files
Reads many legacy and layered formats macOS does not open natively
Interface translated into about 30 languages, with right-to-left support for Arabic and Hebrew
caveats: Not yet notarized by Apple, so first launch needs approval under System Settings > Privacy & Security
Animated GIF support is listed as coming next
Page says the first release is on its way, so it may not yet be available as a downloadable release
